instruction: I'm reviewing my friend's course outline. Please make the second paragraph bold to emphasize the course introduction section.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully selected the last paragraph and applied strikethrough formatting via Format > Text > Strikethrough menu, then saved the document.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer menus, select text paragraphs using click+Ctrl+Shift+End, apply text formatting via Format menu, save documents with Ctrl+S.
metadata.task_rationale: Variation tests bold formatting instead of strikethrough, targeting a different paragraph. Same document setup and similar formatting workflow.
metadata.explanation: Task asks agent to bold the second paragraph. Getter reads the docx and checks bold ratio of runs in the second non-empty paragraph. Metric checks if at least 90% of characters are bold.

scoring_breakdown.bold_formatting: 1.0 - At least 90% of second paragraph characters are bold

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the second non-empty paragraph (paragraph_index=1, 0-indexed) from the docx file, matching the instruction's 'second paragraph'.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('min_bold_ratio', 0.9)), properly handling the rule type where expected IS the rules dict.
Postconfig properly saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest state.
Single instruction requirement (bold second paragraph) is fully covered by the evaluator.
Partial credit logic (bold_ratio / min_ratio) is reasonable for intermediate results.

Minor concern: run.font.bold in python-docx returns None for style-inherited bold (not explicitly set), which would be counted as non-bold. In practice, applying bold via Ctrl+B in LibreOffice sets explicit bold on runs, so this is unlikely to cause issues but is a theoretical edge case.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking run.font.bold is not False (i.e., treat None as potentially bold if the paragraph style is bold) to handle style-inherited bold formatting edge cases.
